boundaries: after a clause terminator (. ; : ! ?) followed by whitespace
immediately before an enumerator, wherever it appears
after a comma followed by whitespace
neverSplitInside: a detected quantitative value - 'March 31, 2030' and '$5,000,000' stay in one unit so the value can be attributed to the span that holds it
whyCommas: A comma-delimited aside is where drafting hides a qualifier inside a lead-in ('... plus, without duplication and to the extent deducted, the sum of'). Splitting there costs nothing - glue-only fragments classify as STRUCTURAL_NOISE - and it stops a lead-in's discharge from ever reaching a qualifier.

shortClausePolicy.rule: There is no length floor anywhere in the detection path. A 15-character clause is a unit exactly like a 200-character one.
shortClausePolicy.howNoiseIsSeparated: by CONTENT, not by length: a fragment whose words are all closed-class (enumerators, punctuation, function words, subordinating connectives, adverbial adjuncts, arithmetic connectives) and which carries no quantitative value is STRUCTURAL_NOISE. Every content word in the language sits outside that closed class, so a proposition can never fall into it.
shortClausePolicy.whyTheOldExperimentFailed: Lowering the v2 floor from 40 to 24 made colon-terminated lead-ins fire as gaps across eleven corpus scenarios. The cause was structural - the segmenter treated a lead-in as a standalone semantic unit - and is fixed here by parent/child ownership, not by another threshold.

ownership.rule: The parent of an enumerated unit is the nearest preceding non-enumerated unit, with or without a colon (real drafting runs '... shall be (a) ... (b) ...' inline as often as '... as follows:').
ownership.direction: Credit flows CHILD -> PARENT only. A covered parent never discharges an uncovered child - that was the audit's Lien carve-out failure.
guards: descent requires EVERY child to be accounted
descent is refused when the lead-in residue carries a quantitative value
descent discharges only the immediate lead-in unit, so a substantive main clause separated by a comma stays accountable
